cors_misconfiguration.summary: Flowise default CORS middleware allows arbitrary origins
cors_misconfiguration.description: GitHub Security Lab reported a CORS misconfiguration in Flowise. The server invokes the CORS middleware with the default open policy, allowing Access-Control-Allow-Origin for arbitrary origins. The primary advisory states that arbitrary origins can connect to the application and that the policy can be chained with sensitive API behavior to read information. This source is used only to create an inert reflected/untrusted-origin response fixture and trusted-origin controls; no live cross-origin request is executed.

mass_assignment.summary: Rails Strong Parameters bypass can pass an untrusted admin property into model update
mass_assignment.description: The official Ruby on Rails security advisory for CVE-2020-8164 describes a Strong Parameters bypass in ActionPack. User-supplied request parameters can escape the intended trusted parameter filtering when application code returns the underlying untrusted hash from each/each_value/each_pair. The advisory's impacted example explicitly includes an attacker-controlled is_admin: true property and passes the resulting parameters to User.update. This provides a direct writable privileged-property acceptance surface for a Mass Assignment/BOPLA raw fixture, with a rejected-property control and unchanged-property near miss.

server_side_template_injection.summary: Apache OFBiz FreeMarker rendering accepts untrusted server-side template expressions
server_side_template_injection.description: GitHub Security Lab reported Server-Side Template Injection in Apache OFBiz. Untrusted request data reached a FreeMarker macro/template rendering path, allowing injected template expressions to be evaluated server-side. The primary advisory documents the request parameter flow into renderLookupField and the resulting server template execution condition. This source is converted only into an inert template-render/error fixture and secure controls; no expression is executed by the benchmark collector.

note: All three external primary candidates were checked against Golden v3, Golden v4, raw v1, raw v2, and the complete v2 candidate inventory before use; root and URL overlap were zero. No detector scoring was used to select these sources.
